title: Routing Grid Shortest Path

statement.md: A grid of network cells has open cells `.` and blocked cells `#`. A packet starts in the top-left cell and must reach the bottom-right cell, moving one step at a time up, down, left or right through open cells.
Print the smallest number of steps, or `-1` if the destination cannot be reached. If either end cell is blocked, the answer is `-1`. A grid with one cell that is open needs 0 steps.

inputFormat: First line: $R$ and $C$. Then $R$ lines of $C$ characters, `.` or `#`.
hints: Every step costs the same, so the first time a cell is reached is by a shortest route.
Mark a cell as seen when it is pushed, not when it is popped, or cells get queued many times.

editorial.md: Breadth-first search from the start with a distance array. Pop a cell, push each unseen open neighbour with distance plus one, and stop when the target is popped. Marking cells when pushed keeps each cell in the queue once, so the time is $O(RC)$. Depth-first search does not give shortest routes in an unweighted grid.

solutions.python:
import sys
from collections import deque


def main():
    tok = sys.stdin.read().split()
    R, C = int(tok[0]), int(tok[1])
    g = tok[2:2 + R]
    if g[0][0] == '#' or g[R - 1][C - 1] == '#':
        print(-1)
        return
    dist = [[-1] * C for _ in range(R)]
    dist[0][0] = 0
    q = deque([(0, 0)])
    while q:
        i, j = q.popleft()
        if (i, j) == (R - 1, C - 1):
            break
        for a, b in ((i + 1, j), (i - 1, j), (i, j + 1), (i, j - 1)):
            if 0 <= a < R and 0 <= b < C and g[a][b] == '.' and dist[a][b] < 0:
                dist[a][b] = dist[i][j] + 1
                q.append((a, b))
    print(dist[R - 1][C - 1])


main()
